note: Whole-to-part (Law 10): phonetics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. The accepted phonetics definition carves it as a human-made discipline of linguistics studying the physical properties of speech sounds. Sibling precedent: linguistics CONTAINS phonology, syntax, morphology, semantics, pragmatics all accepted in this turn. Phonetics is the classical sibling discipline of phonology.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): semantics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Accepted pattern mirrors linguistics CONTAINS phonology (Ezra, accepted): the accepted linguistics definition explicitly names semantics as one of its constituent subfields alongside phonology, morphology, syntax, and pragmatics. Semantics is a part of linguistics conceptual structure.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): historical-linguistics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Per its accepted definition, historical-linguistics is a disciplinary framework for reconstructing diachronic change in language systems from attested corpora — one of the named subfields of the parent discipline. The accepted linguistics definition explicitly names 'historical linguistics' among its named subdisciplines. Parallel to accepted edges: linguistics CONTAINS phonology, semantics, pragmatics, morphology, syntax, phonetics. Pinned sense: historical-linguistics as the subdiscipline of language change over time.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9): is computational-linguistics a specific kind of linguistics? Yes. Per its accepted definition, it is a disciplinary framework for formalizing linguistic knowledge in algorithms and computational models — a specific subfield of the general discipline. Nearest accepted kind: linguistics (no intermediate kind). Pinned sense: computational-linguistics as the subdiscipline of computational language analysis.

CONTAINS = part-of, pinned to the discipline-as-collection sense: the board already ACCEPTED linguistics CONTAINS sociolinguistics, historical-linguistics, and psycholinguistics, and INSTANCE_OF computational-linguistics -> linguistics; this files the fourth containment the family pattern implies, completing the set of subfields held inside the discipline.

Psycholinguistics investigates the cognitive mechanisms underlying language use — perception, production, acquisition, and representation. The removal test passes: remove cognition and psycholinguistics has no subject matter to operate on. This is not a meta-level claim (Law 2b); it is an object-level dependency where the discipline's entire investigative apparatus targets cognitive processes.

Pinned sense: phase-locked vocoder as STFT-based algorithm with analysis/synthesis window length and hop size parameters. Removal test (Law 8): remove the Hann window function — the specific window shape used for spectral leakage control and overlap-add reconstruction — and the STFT frames the vocoder operates on lose their defined spectral leakage properties and overlap-add consistency; the algorithm's phase-locking rule operates on frames that no longer reconstruct correctly. The vocoder stops operating as a phase-coherent time-stretch/pitch-shift tool. Dependency is object-level material requirement for the STFT stage, not sayability.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): pragmatics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Accepted pattern mirrors linguistics CONTAINS phonology (Ezra, accepted): the accepted linguistics definition explicitly names pragmatics as one of its constituent subfields alongside phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Pragmatics is a part of linguistics conceptual structure.

Linguistic register is a specific subfield/concept within linguistics, the study of language varieties. It is a specific kind of linguistic object, not a part. INSTANCE_OF pins specific → general. The entry's scope describes language varieties, which is a topic linguistics studies.

Syntax is a specific component of grammar: a competent linguist calls syntax 'a part of grammar' or 'grammatical syntax'. Grammar is the broader system of rules for a language, encompassing syntax, morphology, phonology, etc. Direction specific→general is correct.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): psycholinguistics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Per its accepted definition, psycholinguistics is a disciplinary framework for mapping mental representations and processes underlying language production, comprehension, and acquisition — one of the named subfields of the parent discipline. The accepted linguistics definition explicitly names 'psycholinguistics' among its named subdisciplines. Parallel to accepted edges: linguistics CONTAINS phonology, semantics, pragmatics, morphology, syntax, phonetics. Pinned sense: psycholinguistics as the subdiscipline of cognitive language processing.

Direction test (Law 9): discourse is a specific kind of linguistics — the subdiscipline studying language use beyond the sentence level, including conversation structure, coherence, and contextual meaning. A competent linguist calls discourse analysis "a part of linguistics" or "discourse linguistics." INSTANCE_OF runs specific→general, and linguistics is the nearest accepted kind. Pinned sense: discourse as the linguistics subdiscipline of language use in context.

Historical linguistics studies language change across time. The removal test passes: remove chronology (the ordered sequence of temporal events) and historical linguistics loses its temporal dimension entirely, ceasing to operate as a discipline. Pinned sense: chronology as the framework of ordered temporal relations that makes historical analysis possible.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9): is psycholinguistics a specific kind of linguistics? Yes. Per its accepted definition, it is a disciplinary framework for mapping the mental representations and processes underlying language production, comprehension, and acquisition — a specific subfield of the general discipline. Nearest accepted kind: linguistics (no intermediate kind). Pinned sense: psycholinguistics as the subdiscipline of cognitive language processing.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): historical-linguistics per its accepted definition as a disciplinary framework for reconstructing diachronic change in language systems from attested corpora. DEPENDS_ON removal test (Law 8b): remove language — the language systems that historical linguistics reconstructs and the attested corpora it uses — and the discipline loses its entire domain. Without language there are no diachronic changes to reconstruct, no attested corpora, no comparative method, no sound change laws. The discipline's operations have nothing to operate on. Object-level dependency on language. Sibling precedent: morphology DEPENDS_ON language, phonology DEPENDS_ON language.

Grammar as a linguistic system comprises several component sub-systems: phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Phonology (the study of sound patterns) is literally a part within the grammatical system — one of its core components. Whole-and-part relation: grammar CONTAINS phonology as a constitutive sub-system.

An argument is a structured reasoning construct consisting of premises and a conclusion. Premises ARE literal parts of an argument — the supporting claims that, together with the conclusion, constitute the argument's structure. Remove the premises and the argument collapses; they are constitutive components within the whole. Whole-and-part relation: argument CONTAINS premise.

Removal test (Law 8b): historical-linguistics' accepted definition carves its object as 'reconstructing diachronic change in language systems from attested corpora.' Remove language and the discipline has no subject matter — no language systems to reconstruct, no sound change laws to state, no attested corpora to analyze. It ceases to operate as a discipline. Same shape as the accepted morphology DEPENDS_ON language: subdiscipline depends on its carved subject matter.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): psycholinguistics per its accepted definition as a disciplinary framework for mapping the mental representations and processes underlying language production, comprehension, and acquisition. DEPENDS_ON removal test (Law 8b): remove language — the mental representations and processes that psycholinguistics maps — and the discipline loses its entire domain. Without language there are no production/comprehension/acquisition processes to study, no lexical access patterns, no syntactic parsing, no processing models, no developmental stages. The discipline's operations collapse. Object-level dependency on language. Sibling precedent: morphology DEPENDS_ON language, phonology DEPENDS_ON language.

Removal test (Law 8b): sociolinguistics' accepted definition carves its object as 'mapping systematic correlations between linguistic variation and social structure.' Remove language and the discipline has no subject matter — no linguistic variables to correlate with social structure. It ceases to operate as a discipline. Same shape as the accepted morphology DEPENDS_ON language: subdiscipline depends on its carved subject matter.

Morphology studies word formation and the structure of words from morphemes. Lexicon is the stored inventory of words and morphemes that morphology operates upon. Removal test: remove the lexicon and morphology has no material to analyze or combine — no stored forms to decompose or build. The dependency is constitutive: morphology is the study and manipulation of lexically stored morphological material.

Discourse is the phenomenon of language extended beyond single utterances — it is inherently a form of communication. Removal test: remove communication and discourse ceases to operate, since discourse IS multi-utterance communication. The dependency is constitutive at the object level: discourse is not merely associated with communication; it is communication operating over extended stretches of talk/text.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9): is sociolinguistics a specific kind of linguistics? Yes. Per its accepted definition, it is a disciplinary framework for mapping systematic correlations between linguistic variation and social structure — a specific subfield of the general discipline. Nearest accepted kind: linguistics (no intermediate kind). Pinned sense: sociolinguistics as the subdiscipline of social language variation.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): morphology is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Accepted pattern mirrors linguistics CONTAINS phonology (Ezra, accepted): the discipline definition explicitly names morphology as one of its constituent subfields. Morphology is a part of linguistics conceptual and institutional structure.

Removal test (Law 8b): psycholinguistics' accepted definition carves its object as 'mapping the mental representations and processes underlying language production, comprehension, and acquisition.' Remove language and the discipline has no subject matter — no production, comprehension, or acquisition to study. It ceases to operate as a discipline. Same shape as the accepted morphology DEPENDS_ON language: subdiscipline depends on its carved subject matter.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): morpheme per its accepted definition as the minimal meaningful unit of a language. DEPENDS_ON removal test (Law 8b): remove language — the system of structured signs in which morphemes exist as minimal meaningful units — and the category has no domain to operate in. Per its own definition, a morpheme is language-relative: its identity as a minimal meaningful unit is constituted by the grammatical system of a specific language. Without language, the morpheme loses its entire parameter set (minimality, meaningfulness, language-relativity) and ceases to operate as the unit it is. Not generic: this is not the meta-level claim that 'concepts need language to be said.' This is object-level: the morpheme's carve is specifically about language's grammatical system. Sibling precedent: lexeme DEPENDS_ON language (accepted pattern). This matches the board's accepted pattern: morphology DEPENDS_ON language, phonology DEPENDS_ON language, linguistics DEPENDS_ON language — each is a discipline or category whose object is language itself.

Removal test (Law 8): remove language — speech-acts cease to operate. A speech-act is an utterance that performs an action (promising, asserting, commanding, etc.). Its entire nature is linguistic — it is an act constituted by language use. Removing language removes the medium through which speech-acts are performed, constituted, and recognized. This is object-level: speech-acts are defined as linguistic actions, not as general actions that happen to sometimes use language.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): sociolinguistics per its accepted definition as a disciplinary framework for mapping systematic correlations between linguistic variation and social structure. DEPENDS_ON removal test (Law 8b): remove language — the system of linguistic variation that sociolinguistics maps — and the discipline loses its entire domain. Without language there are no speech communities, no social variables, no linguistic variables, no interactional context to study. The discipline's operations have nothing to operate on. This is object-level, not meta-level: the sociolinguistics definition specifically carves language as its subject matter, not just any domain. Sibling precedent: the accepted morphology DEPENDS_ON language, phonology DEPENDS_ON language, linguistics DEPENDS_ON language — each is a discipline whose domain is language.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): syntax is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Accepted pattern mirrors linguistics CONTAINS phonology (Ezra, accepted): the accepted linguistics definition explicitly names syntax as one of its constituent subfields alongside phonology, morphology, semantics, and pragmatics. Syntax is a part of linguistics conceptual structure.

Grammar is the whole system of rules for a language, and syntax is one of its constituent components (alongside morphology, phonology, semantics). Grammar contains syntax in the part-of sense of Law 10: syntax is a part inside the whole grammar. Pinned sense: grammar as a structured system of linguistic rules, syntax as its sentence-structure subcomponent.

INSTANCE_OF test (Law 9): is historical-linguistics a specific kind of linguistics? Yes. Per its accepted definition, it is a disciplinary framework for reconstructing diachronic change in language systems from attested corpora — a specific subfield of the general discipline. Nearest accepted kind: linguistics (no intermediate kind). Pinned sense: historical-linguistics as the subdiscipline of language change over time.

Computational linguistics uses computational models and algorithms to study language processing, acquisition, and structure. The removal test passes: remove computation and computational linguistics has no methodology to operate with. Pinned sense: computation as the formal manipulation of symbols according to rules, which is the constitutive methodology of computational linguistics.

Removal test (Law 8): remove language — phrases cease to operate. A phrase is a linguistic unit: a group of words functioning as a coherent unit within a sentence. Its entire existence and operation is within a language system. Removing language removes all linguistic units — phrases, words, morphemes — because they are constitutive parts of language, not merely concepts that need language to be described. This is object-level (Law 2b): phrase is defined by its position within language, not by its status as a concept that happens to be linguistic.

Language operates through symbols — signs that stand for something within a conventionally shared system. The removal test passes: remove symbol (a sign that conventionally represents something other than itself) and language loses its fundamental medium of operation. Pinned sense: symbol as an abstract sign-representation relation, which is constitutive of language as a symbolic communication system.

Knowledge is classically defined as justified true belief — belief is a constitutive component within the whole. You cannot have knowledge without belief: belief is the propositional-attitude component that, together with justification and truth, constitutes knowledge. This is a part-whole relation: knowledge CONTAINS belief as one of its necessary components.

Language is a structured system composed of several components: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and vocabulary. Vocabulary (the inventory of words) is literally a PART within this system — one of the core components alongside grammar. This is a whole-and-part relation: language CONTAINS vocabulary as one of its constitutive subsystems.

Removal test (Law 8b): computational-linguistics' accepted definition carves its object as formalizing linguistic knowledge in algorithms and computational models. Remove language and the discipline has no subject matter — no corpora to process, no linguistic models to build, no language phenomena to analyze. It ceases to operate as a discipline. Same shape as the accepted morphology DEPENDS_ON language: subdiscipline depends on its carved subject matter.

Cognition is the broad set of mental processes including perception, attention, reasoning, and memory. Memory is literally a component of cognition — one of the core mental faculties that cognition encompasses. Removal of memory doesn't stop cognition (other faculties remain), but memory is a constitutive PART within the whole of cognition, making this a clear CONTAINS (whole-and-part) relation.

Whole-to-part (Law 10): sociolinguistics is a structural subcomponent of linguistics. Per its accepted definition, sociolinguistics is a disciplinary framework for mapping systematic correlations between linguistic variation and social structure — one of the named subfields of the parent discipline. The accepted linguistics definition explicitly names 'sociolinguistics' among its named subdisciplines. Parallel to accepted edges: linguistics CONTAINS phonology, semantics, pragmatics, morphology, syntax, phonetics. Pinned sense: sociolinguistics as the subdiscipline of social language variation.

Memory as a cognitive faculty comprises several component processes: encoding, storage, and retrieval (recall). Recall is literally a part of the memory system — one of its core operational processes. This is a whole-and-part relation: the memory system CONTAINS recall as one of its constitutive processes.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): computational-linguistics per its accepted definition as a disciplinary framework for formalizing linguistic knowledge in algorithms and computational models. DEPENDS_ON removal test (Law 8b): remove language — the linguistic knowledge that computational linguistics formalizes in algorithms and models — and the discipline loses its entire domain. Without language there are no corpora to design, no statistical models for, no symbolic grammars to build, no evaluation metrics, no processing pipelines. The discipline's operations have nothing to operate on. Object-level dependency on language. Sibling precedent: morphology DEPENDS_ON language, phonology DEPENDS_ON language.

Direction test (Law 9): grammar is a specific kind of syntax — a structured set of rules governing word arrangement and sentence formation. A competent linguist calls grammar "a syntax" or "the syntactic system" of a language. INSTANCE_OF runs specific→general, and syntax is the nearest accepted kind. Pinned sense: grammar as the rule-governed system of syntactic structure, not the broader discipline of linguistics.
